A read-only text viewer. No accounts, ads, analytics, or network permission.

History and open documents store references and reading preferences, not document contents. Sharing or opening a file with another app creates a temporary copy. Old copies are cleaned on the next app start or share after 24 hours; only the latest 20 are kept.

Open file
Choose a document through Android’s system picker. This is also the fallback when another app does not offer Textr.

Open with and Share
In a file manager or another app, select a file, choose Open with or Share, then choose Textr. Shared text can also be viewed. Textr’s own Share file and Open with actions send a read-only copy to another app.

Choosing a default
When Android offers Always, you can select Textr as the default. The available choices depend on the sending app and the reported file type (MIME type), not just the filename extension. Some apps always use their own viewer. Textr cannot force an association for every extension.

Unavailable recent files
Recent files and open documents store references, not contents. A moved or deleted file, or an expired temporary permission, may require you to select it again using Open file. Clearing history does not delete your files.

Older text files
If text cannot be decoded or looks wrong, try Reopen with encoding. Your choice only changes how Textr reads the bytes; it does not convert the file.

Offline viewing
Textr has no network permission. A document provider selected in the system picker may independently use the network to retrieve your file.
Keep open and recent files beside the reader on an unfolded phone or tablet. The sidebar hides when space is limited or system text is enlarged.
